completion_criteria.text: hooks/lib/pre-tool-use.mjs inverted to deny-by-default inside a protected root: any resolvable token under a protected root DENIES unless the segment head is on an explicit read-only allowlist. shell-tokens.mjs left unchanged.

Both directions proven by committed tests: all 12 verified evasions (including `( rm -rf <root> )` and `sudo rm -rf <root>`) assert DENY, and the 41-command read-only corpus asserts ALLOW. Red-before/green-after evidence recorded.
The scanSegments blow-up resolved so the guard fails CLOSED on oversized or pathological input, never open, with a test asserting the fail-closed path at the boundary.
Full plugin test suite green on the branch, and a fresh code-reviewer plus security-reviewer pass over the final diff returns no CRITICAL or HIGH findings.

Branch merged to main, plugin published to the marketplace, and re-installed globally - then a live end-to-end check against the real store shows a real evasion DENIED and ordinary read commands still ALLOWED.

spine.active_goal: REVERSED 2026-07-27: the parser is DELETED, not hardened. The real store is git commits on refs/heads/_ledger in the project's .git; the guarded $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA dir is a disposable worktree the plugin rm -rf's and rebuilds every init. Verified by execution: the parser ALLOWS git branch -D _ledger, update-ref -d, push origin :_ledger and PATH=/tmp cat ROOT/f but DENIES rm -rf ROOT. It guards the throwaway copy. Protection is recoverability, not prevention.
spine.next_step: IMPLEMENT in DevLabs/continuity-ledger-plugin (NOT .windful-ocean), in order. (1) DELETE command-allowlist, command-scope, shell-tokens, shell-source, token-access and the unit/scope machinery in pre-tool-use.mjs plus their tests; KEEP the Write/Edit path deny, ledger-tool auto-approve, resolveLedgerRoots, hook-io fail-closed. (2) REPLACE per 0029: tripwire, root or _ledger substring -> ask, no parsing. (3) FIX LocalDriver per 0030. (4) README on sandbox denyWrite. FIRST decide branch topology.
open_risks: The tripwire asks on ANY mention of a ledger path, including legitimate reads. Accepted friction under the accident-only threat model (0028). Do NOT add exceptions to quieten it - carving out exceptions is exactly how parsing crept in the first time.

Recoverability depends on per-mutation commit and the Stop-hook push firing. No-remote repos, or an agent that disables hooks before destroying ref plus remote, degrade a recoverable store to an unrecoverable one. A mirror outside the repo is the fix if ever scoped.

A determined same-uid agent is explicitly NOT covered and cannot be, for the _ledger ref inside .git - the agent must retain normal git rights over that directory. Accepted per 0028; replicas, not prevention.

BRANCH TOPOLOGY UNDECIDED: 18 commits on fix/pre-tool-use-guard are largely to be reverted. Choose a fresh branch off b60ac56 versus reverts on the existing branch. That history is the audit trail for WHY the parser died - do not discard it silently.

COMPLETION CRITERIA ARE STALE: 1 and 2 are done but describe the deleted parser; 3 is parser-framed; 5 asserts a live evasion is DENIED, which the tripwire answers with ask. Only 4 survives as written. Re-derive the set before any DoD close; do not toggle the old ones.

NON-GIT IS THE ONLY UNPROTECTED STORE (verified: LocalDriver commit/sync are no-op stubs at local-driver.mjs:183-189). Until item 3 ships, rm -rf is permanent there, while the recoverable git store absorbed all 23 commits of attention.
UNAUTHORIZED DEFECT, still open, do not fix without explicit go: the Stop hook nags every turn (stop.mjs exits 2 unconditionally, never reads stop_hook_active).
Deleting ~790 lines will drop the suite count sharply from 735. Expected, not a regression - those tests only proved the parser's own fixed vectors stayed fixed.
